title: Old Savoy Home Back In Hands Of First Owners — Page 12, The Denison Herald, Thursday, Oct. 2, 1952
text:
Page 12—THE DENISON HERALD—Thursday, Oct. 2, 1952

86-YEAR-OLD SAVOY HOME—This house was originally built in 1866, but recently was moved into Savoy and remodeled. It is now owned by Mrs. W. R. Jones, a great-granddaughter of its original builder. (Staff Photo)

Old Savoy Home Back In Hands Of First Owners

SAVOY— James Wrenn would never recognize the house that his great granddaughter, Mrs. W. R. Jones, is living in today as the same one that he constructed at the end of the Civil War in 1865.

The house recently was remodeled, but the old original beams and sills that were hauled by oxen and wagon from East Texas are still intact.

Since Wrenn built the house, it has been moved to a new site and out of the possession of his family. But today it is back in the same family, albeit with a modern 1952 face.

Mrs. H. A. Ooten, a granddaughter of Wrenn, told how Wrenn had fought his way through the Civil War as a member of the "Confederate Missourians.". The womenfolk in his family came to Texas during the war and he followed later.

They settled in Savoy and hauled the lumber to build the house by oxen and cart from East Texas, a three-week trip with each load.

After his death in 1888, a daughter and son-in-law, Mr. and Mrs. Robert Blakey, moved in. Incidentally, Mrs. Blakey, who was Rebecca Wrenn, lives north of Savoy with a son, Tommy. She is 84.

After the Blakeys moved out, one of their sons, Clyde, moved in and stayed there until he sold the house to Earl Reed. Reed, in turn, had the house brought into Savoy and then sold it to Tommy Hall.

It was Hall who remodeled it and then sold it to Mrs. Jones, a great-granddaughter of its original builder.

SAVOY,—Apprentice Seaman B. F. Wade who entered service Feb. 2, is receiving preliminary training in the navy at San Diego, Cal. He is the son of Mrs. Della Wade of this community. Born at Savoy, Seaman Wade was graduated from Savoy High School in 1944. He was employed by the Standard Oil Co. prior to entering service.

SAVOY.—Messman W. D. Crawford, Merchant Marine, has been transferred from St. Petersburg, Fla., to Houston. He is now home on furlough visiting his wife, the former Miss Joie Kirtpatrick, and his father, G. D. Crawford, Fort Worth. Messman Crawford entered service Dec. 31, 1944, and in civilian life, was a farmer.

Savoy

Cpl Troy McKinney, Camp Livingston, La. is spending a 11 day furlough with his mother, Mrs. Tim Short, before being transferred to Camp Cook, Cal. Pvt. Trueman McKinney, Camp Maxey, and Miss Mary Jesse McKinney, Dallas have also been guests in the home.

Clarence Rino, of the U. S. Navy, with his wife of Dallas have been visiting his parents Mr. and Mrs. Ernest Rino.

Mr. and Mrs. E. E. Patton and children have returned from Wich[ita]
